gloss: way of reading; pronunciation of a character

definitions.gloss: way of reading; how to read
definitions.explanation: The method or manner in which something is read, including the pronunciation assigned to a kanji character or the interpretation of a text.
A particular way of interpreting or making sense of a situation, data, or written material.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}み{方|かた}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me how to read this kanji.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}の{読|よ}み{方|かた}が{難|むずか}しくて、よく{間違|まちが}えられる。
examples.english: The reading of my name is difficult, so people often get it wrong.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{読|よ}み{方|かた}には{音読|おんよ}みと{訓読|くんよ}みがある。
examples.english: Japanese characters have two types of readings: on'yomi and kun'yomi.

examples.japanese: データの{読|よ}み{方|かた}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: The interpretation of the data is different.

examples.japanese: {同|おな}じニュースでも{人|ひと}によって{読|よ}み{方|かた}が{変|か}わる。
examples.english: Even for the same news, the interpretation varies depending on the person.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}の{流|なが}れの{読|よ}み{方|かた}は{経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}まないと{身|み}につかない。
examples.english: Learning to read the flow of a match only comes with accumulated experience.

notes:
{読|よ}み{方|かた} follows the productive ～{方|かた} (way of doing) pattern attached to the verb stem of {読|よ}む.

Sense 1 is especially common in language-learning contexts when asking about kanji pronunciation. Sense 2 extends to interpreting data, situations, or texts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}み{方|かた} (how to read a kanji)
- {名前|なまえ}の{読|よ}み{方|かた} (reading of a name)
- {地図|ちず}の{読|よ}み{方|かた} (how to read a map)
- データの{読|よ}み{方|かた} (how to interpret data)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {発音|はつおん}: pronunciation in general, not limited to reading
- {解釈|かいしゃく}: interpretation, more formal and analytical
